test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The selling price of 40 books is equal to the cost price of 30 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **Selling Price** of 'x' articles equals the **Cost Price** of 'y' articles.

Gain or Loss percentage = (y − x) ÷ x × 100%.

Here x = 40 (articles sold) and y = 30 (articles costed).

Percentage = (30 − 40) ÷ 40 × 100% = −10 ÷ 40 × 100% = −25%.

The negative sign indicates a **Loss**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP of 40 books = CP of 30 books.
**Formulas:** Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 | SP/CP ratio method.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/513586b1ce4bbbc01cfd0e326706197a15cae868bc78e716e261e907b5382299.png] 
⇒ Let CP of 1 book be Re. 1.
⇒ CP of 40 books = Rs. 40.
⇒ Given: SP of 40 books = CP of 30 books = Rs. 30.
⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 40 − 30 = Rs. 10.
⇒ Loss% = (10 ÷ 40) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) vs Selling Price (SP)

When CP > SP, there is a **Loss**. Loss% = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100. Always calculate profit or loss on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

Ratio Method

Express the relation as a ratio: 40 × SP = 30 × CP ⇒ SP ÷ CP = 30 ÷ 40 = 3 ÷ 4. This directly shows that for every 4 units of cost, there is 1 unit of loss.</p
